summary: Iteration 11 (strictly READ-ONLY, GET only): full portal endpoint coverage and the Retailers feature. Backend: new tests/test_portal_endpoints_retailers.py, 38/38 passed. All 25 listed GET endpoints return 200 through the proxy (including the CSV exports leads-export/csv and reports/export, which are text/csv), and so do the local /roles and /admin-users. Unauthenticated GETs return 401. The counts are exact: properties 55, agents 27, platform-users 150, leads 24, transactions 12. Grouping /marketplace/products by retailer_id gives 6 retailers: Pointek 12 products/6 in stock/6 out/0 unknown, Fouani 25/22/3/0, BoConcept 23/0/0/23, Furniture House 17/0/0/17, SLOT 14/14/0/0, Lagom 10/0/0/10. The Lead Sources pie renders 4 sectors. Properties, Property Verification, Agents and Users have no lock icon. There are 6 retailer cards sorted Pointek (6 out), Fouani (3 out), then the rest by product count, and their numbers match the API exactly. Pointek detail: stats 12/6/6/0, an alert with 6 items, 12 rows with the 6 out-of-stock rows first, and all images load. The back button works, an unknown id shows retailer-not-found, and SLOT has no alert. Every page in the sweep loaded with no 4xx/5xx and no page errors: Properties 55 rows (coloured badges for available, premium, sold, coming soon and verified, with 'Coming Soon' spaced), Property Verification 3, Agents 27 (22 Legacy badges, 27 level lines), Users 150, Leads 24, Transactions 12 (11 via Paystack, 1 via Flutterwave), and Payments, Tokens, Marketplace, Notifications, App Config, Analytics, Reports, Media, Roles and Settings all load. Mobile 390px: the Dashboard and retailer detail have no overflow. The Retailers list overflowed (420px), which I fixed. No live data was modified.

critical_code_review_comments: portal_proxy: GET /api/media/file/* skips auth by design (public media). This is fine for images, but make sure the portal never serves private documents (for example property verification docs) under that path.

Retailers.jsx and OutOfStockBanner each call useMarketplaceProducts, which fetches the full product list on every mount (Dashboard plus Retailers). This is acceptable at 101 products. Consider caching or a shared context if the catalogue grows.

Retailers detail sort only ranks out_of_stock < unknown < in_stock. There is no secondary sort (for example by title), so the order within a group follows the API order. That is fine but not deterministic.
